title: Career roadmap · Innovation Strategist
summary: Build from science and technology policy research into innovation-system analysis, technology foresight, R&D strategy, public policy, intellectual property and organisational innovation.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. Early years develop policy research, economics, quantitative analysis and technology assessment; later years focus on innovation portfolios, institutional strategy, technology translation and senior advisory work.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Develop expertise in innovation systems, STI policy, R&D economics, technology assessment, data analysis and evidence-based policy.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Own a strategic domain such as emerging technology, industrial innovation, research policy, technology transfer or national innovation systems.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead innovation strategy across governments, research institutions, corporations, investors or technology ecosystems.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine foresight, AI and emerging-technology assessment with R&D portfolio strategy, economic policy and institutional transformation.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Maintain strong policy and analytical foundations while learning to evaluate AI, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, quantum technologies, climate technologies and other emerging fields. The senior strategist's value comes from connecting technical possibilities with economic, institutional, regulatory and societal consequences.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → STI Policy/Innovation Analyst → Innovation Strategist → Senior Strategist/Consultant → Innovation Program Manager → Strategy Director → Chief Innovation Strategist / Innovation Practice Head

items: 15+ years, with variation by sector and organization
blocks.label: Typical planning ranges are

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior Innovation Strategist should be able to evaluate technologies before they become mainstream and translate that assessment into investment, policy or organizational decisions. Maintain analytical depth while developing expertise in AI governance, biotechnology, climate technology, advanced manufacturing, quantum technologies, R&D portfolio management and technology commercialization. The strongest profile connects scientific possibilities with economic and institutional realities.
